Veigar.laning: Early on, clear the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and secure last hits with Ryze Q Overload to protect your growth. Stand behind minions so you don’t take Veigar Q Baleful Strike for no reason and give him growth stacks.
Veigar.phase: Early on, Veigar has few growth stacks and no mobility, giving you chances to pressure him, but Ryze also lacks mana and damage, so protect your farm and look for short trades. In the mid and late game, Ryze’s combos become strong once he has sufficient levels and core items that provide mana. Veigar’s stacks grow permanently, making him stronger as the game goes on, so check your positioning and whether Veigar E Event Horizon is available more carefully as the game gets longer.
Veigar.teamfight: Join after your allies engage, spread Ryze E Spell Flux marks across the frontline, and deal area damage with Ryze Q Overload. Before starting a fight around an objective, check Veigar’s position and whether Veigar E Event Horizon is available. Use Ryze R Realm Warp to bring allies together or disengage after a team fight, and tell the allies who will travel with you in advance.
Veigar.watch: Veigar E Event Horizon stuns you when you cross its edge, so if you’re trapped inside, don’t run into the edge; move around inside and wait. Veigar W Dark Matter shows where it will land, so keep moving to dodge it. Veigar R Primordial Burst deals more damage based on your missing health, so if you’re below half health, get out of range.

Vex.build: Ryze’s mana affects his damage and combos, so build a mana-granting core item first. Against Vex’s damage, build magic resistance rather than armor. Also consider movement speed to leave telegraphed attack areas and tenacity.
Vex.combo: To root Vex, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison, in that order. For an all-in, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison → Ryze Q Overload → Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. Ryze Q Overload can be blocked by minions, so time it for when Vex steps outside the wave.
Vex.escape: Hold off on engaging while Vex P Doom 'n Gloom is active, and look for an opening right after Vex uses it on the wave or to poke.
Vex.fight: Right after Vex uses a skill on the wave, trade briefly with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. It’s a chance to engage once Vex P Doom 'n Gloom has been consumed and Vex W Personal Space is down.
Vex.laning: Early on, protect your CS and mana instead of looking for kills. Clear the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and secure last hits with Ryze Q Overload. If your mana is below half, stop fighting and manage the wave only.
Vex.phase: Early on, Ryze lacks mana and damage, so focus on growing instead of looking for kills on Vex. In the mid and late game, once you have core items that provide mana, one full Ryze combo becomes strong. Even then, choose a fight when Vex P Doom 'n Gloom and Vex W Personal Space are down.
Vex.teamfight: Move low-health allies out of Vex’s range first so they aren’t the first kill target of Vex R Shadow Surge. After your allies engage, spread Ryze E Spell Flux across the frontline and deal area damage with Ryze Q Overload. If Vex dives onto an ally hit by Vex R Shadow Surge, root Vex with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Vex.watch: Don’t engage with Ryze R Realm Warp while Vex P Doom 'n Gloom is active. Vex E Looming Darkness grows in size from a distance, so if you’re already within range, dodge a short distance to the side. If Vex R Shadow Surge hits you and marks you, move toward your allies immediately.

Viktor.build: Account for the mana needed for Ryze P Arcane Mastery and your combos by building a mana-granting core item first. Viktor’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance rather than armor.
Viktor.combo: When catching Viktor, root him first with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison. Then use Ryze Q Overload → Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. If you use Ryze W Rune Prison first, it only slows him instead of rooting him.
Viktor.escape: Viktor has no dash, so the window to close the distance opens after Viktor W Gravity Field is down. When approaching with Ryze R Realm Warp, cast from a safe spot, then root him after you arrive with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Viktor.fight: Right after Viktor uses Viktor E Hextech Ray on the wave, trade briefly with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. Once you dodge Viktor W Gravity Field and close the distance, fight by rooting him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Viktor.laning: Early on, clear the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and secure last hits with Ryze Q Overload instead of forcing a kill. If your mana is below half, stop trading and manage the wave.
Viktor.phase: Early on, before Viktor P Glorious Evolution stacks up, you have a chance to pressure him, but Ryze also lacks mana and damage early, so protect your farm and trade briefly. In the mid and late game, Ryze’s mana core items and levels make his combos strong. Viktor’s growth stacks also build permanently, so reassess the outcome of the same engage angle in the late game.
Viktor.teamfight: After your allies engage, spread Ryze E Spell Flux across the frontline and use Ryze Q Overload to deal area damage to the spread marks. Don’t stay inside Viktor W Gravity Field. Use Ryze R Realm Warp to regroup with split allies or disengage after a team fight.
Viktor.watch: Viktor E Hextech Ray is easy to hit if you stand in line with the wave, so stand off to the side. Leave immediately when Viktor W Gravity Field appears, and don’t keep trading inside its area.

Vladimir.build: Build a mana-granting core item so you can make use of Ryze P Arcane Mastery and keep your combos going. Build magic resistance early against Vladimir’s damage. If duels are prolonged, add Grievous Wounds to reduce his healing, and consider Liandry's Torment against a Vladimir who has built a lot of health.
Vladimir.combo: If Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is down, fight with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison → Ryze Q Overload → Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. You need the first Ryze E Spell Flux for Ryze W Rune Prison to root instead of slow. If Vladimir is among minions, Ryze Q Overload can be blocked, so time it for when he steps outside the wave.
Vladimir.escape: The chance to engage comes after Vladimir W Sanguine Pool ends. Cast Ryze R Realm Warp from a safe spot to close the distance, then catch him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Vladimir.fight: Right after Vladimir uses a skill on the wave, trade briefly with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. Bait out Vladimir W Sanguine Pool first, then root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison as it ends. When there’s a chance to close the distance, you can engage with Ryze R Realm Warp.
Vladimir.laning: Early on, clear the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and secure last hits with Ryze Q Overload to protect your growth. If your mana falls below half, stop trading and manage the wave only.
Vladimir.phase: In the mid and late game, Ryze’s combos are strong once he has mana core items, but Vladimir also becomes harder to deal with as he grows. Build on your early lead and fight during the window when Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is down.
Vladimir.teamfight: After your allies engage, spread Ryze E Spell Flux across the frontline and use Ryze Q Overload on the spread marks. Don’t group up where several allies could be hit by Vladimir R Hemoplague. If infected, step back and rejoin after the effect ends.
Vladimir.watch: Vladimir Q Transfusion can prolong a trade with healing and increased movement speed, so hit briefly and back off. When Vladimir E Tides of Blood is charged, keep minions between you or get out of range. Vladimir R Hemoplague increases the damage you take, so re-engage after its effect ends.

Xerath.build: Build a mana-granting core item first to provide the mana needed for Ryze P Arcane Mastery and your combos. Xerath’s main damage is magic, so if you need resistance, build magic resistance instead of armor. Also prioritize a way to deal with the stun from Xerath E Shocking Orb.
Xerath.combo: After engaging, land a guaranteed root with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison, then follow up with Ryze Q Overload → Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. If you use Ryze W Rune Prison first, it only slows, so apply the mark first when catching Xerath.
Xerath.escape: The window to engage opens right after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down. Xerath has no mobility, so close the distance with Ryze R Realm Warp during this window and root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison. Ryze R Realm Warp takes time to activate and disappears if you’re immobilized, so cast it from a safe spot.
Xerath.fight: Early on, focus on farming. Right after Xerath uses a skill on the wave, trade briefly with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. If Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are down, look for a chance to close the distance and fight with Ryze R Realm Warp.
Xerath.laning: Grow by clearing the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and securing last hits with Ryze Q Overload. Farm while avoiding Xerath’s heavy damage and wait for the period when mana runs dry, then push the lane and call your jungler. If Ryze’s mana is below half, stop trading and manage the wave.
Xerath.phase: Early on, Ryze lacks mana and damage, so protect your CS and growth instead of looking for kills.
Xerath.teamfight: After your allies engage, spread Ryze E Spell Flux marks across the frontline and deal area damage with Ryze Q Overload. If you see Xerath R Rite of the Arcane’s cast animation, dodge immediately or engage while Xerath can’t move. Also use Ryze R Realm Warp to join your allies or disengage after a team fight.
Xerath.watch: Xerath Q Arcanopulse passes through minions, so when you see him charging, change direction and dodge to the side. If you’re stunned by Xerath E Shocking Orb, you’re likely to take follow-up damage, so don’t rush to engage while this skill is available.

Yasuo.build: Build Cloth Armor early to survive and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Yasuo’s main damage is physical and Ryze has relatively low armor, so build armor first.
Yasuo.combo: If you need a root, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison, in that order, to root instead of slow. For an all-in, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison → Ryze Q Overload → Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload.
Yasuo.escape: Right after Yasuo throws a Yasuo Q Steel Tempest tornado, he has no way to knock you up for a while, giving you a chance to engage. If Yasuo R Last Breath isn’t ready, close the distance with Ryze R Realm Warp and root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade comes back quickly, so don’t engage just because he used it once.
Yasuo.fight: Strip Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield with a short poke before committing to a full trade. Right after Yasuo throws the Yasuo Q Steel Tempest tornado or uses a skill on the wave, hit briefly with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload, then back off.
Yasuo.laning: Early on, protect your CS and growth instead of looking for kills. Clear the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and secure last hits with Ryze Q Overload. Keeping the wave thin near your side reduces the minions Yasuo E Sweeping Blade can use to approach. If your mana is below half, stop trading and manage the wave only.
Yasuo.phase: Early on, Ryze lacks mana and damage, so focus on farming instead of trying to kill Yasuo. In the mid and late game, once you have core items that provide mana, one full Ryze combo becomes strong. After clearing the wave, join your allies with Ryze R Realm Warp.
Yasuo.teamfight: Join second, after your allies’ engage tools have landed. Spread Ryze E Spell Flux marks across the frontline first, then deal area damage with Ryze Q Overload. If Yasuo knocks you up with Yasuo Q Steel Tempest’s tornado, he can follow up with Yasuo R Last Breath, so move out of its line.
Yasuo.watch: If Yasuo hits you twice in a row with Yasuo Q Steel Tempest, his next Q becomes a tornado that knocks you up, so move to the side to dodge when his stacks are full. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade uses minions to approach, and Yasuo W Wind Wall blocks projectiles, so don’t use key skills in front of the wall.

Yone.build: Build a mana-granting core item first to support Ryze’s growth and combos. Yone deals multiple damage types, and Yone W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on your max health, so don’t rely on building only one type of resistance or health.
Yone.combo: To guarantee a root on Yone, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison, in that order. When there’s a chance to all-in, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison → Ryze Q Overload → Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. When you need to escape, use Ryze E Spell Flux and Ryze W Rune Prison to stack two runes, then use Ryze Q Overload’s movement speed increase.
Yone.escape: Don’t engage just because Yone E Soul Unbound is down; also check Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone R Fate Sealed. Especially before Yone R Fate Sealed is ready again, close the distance with Ryze R Realm Warp from a safe spot and look for a chance to catch him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Yone.fight: Right after Yone uses a skill on the wave, trade briefly with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload, then back off. If Yone dives in with Yone E Soul Unbound, root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison and look for a chance to prevent his return. Don’t walk into range while Yone Q Mortal Steel’s tornado is ready.
Yone.laning: Clear the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and secure last hits with Ryze Q Overload. If your mana falls below half, stop trading and manage the wave.
Yone.phase: In the mid game, choose fights when Yone’s engage tools are down, and push the lane before joining your allies with Ryze R Realm Warp. In the late game, make use of your combo damage once Ryze has the levels and mana core items he needs, while continuing to watch Yone’s tornado and engage path.
Yone.teamfight: Spread out from your allies so Yone W Spirit Cleave’s shield doesn’t grow, and check whether you are alone at the very back along Yone R Fate Sealed’s path. After your allies engage, spread Ryze E Spell Flux across the frontline and deal area damage with Ryze Q Overload. If Yone dives in with Yone E Soul Unbound, root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison and look for a chance to prevent his return.
Yone.watch: When Yone repeatedly hits minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel, he’s preparing his tornado, so keep your distance until the stacks disappear. Save Ryze W Rune Prison for when Yone engages with Yone E Soul Unbound. Yone R Fate Sealed pulls in enemies it hits, so check the engage path and your position in the formation during team fights.

Zed.build: Build Cloth Armor early to survive and choose Plated Steelcaps for your boots. Zed’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. Move Zhonya's Hourglass earlier in your core build to prepare for his engage. Zed P Contempt for the Weak deals magic damage based on your max health, so don’t rely on stacking health alone.
Zed.combo: For an all-in that catches Zed, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison → Ryze Q Overload → Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. If you use Ryze W Rune Prison first, it only slows instead of rooting, so apply the mark with Ryze E Spell Flux first. If you need to escape, use Ryze E Spell Flux and Ryze W Rune Prison to stack two runes, then use Ryze Q Overload’s movement speed increase.
Zed.escape: Don’t engage just because Zed W Living Shadow is down. Before Zed R Death Mark is ready again, close the distance with Ryze R Realm Warp during the opening when Zed W Living Shadow is also down. Then root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Zed.fight: Start a fight after Zed uses Zed W Living Shadow and the shadow disappears, or after Zed has already switched places. For a short trade, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. When you need to catch Zed’s engage, root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Zed.laning: Early on, protect your CS and growth instead of looking for kills. Clear the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and secure last hits with Ryze Q Overload. Poke briefly only right after Zed uses a skill on the wave, and stop trading if your mana falls below half. Ryze Q Overload is blocked by the first target it hits, so use it when Zed is outside the wave.
Zed.phase: Early on, Ryze lacks mana and damage, so focus on growing and don’t give Zed an advantage. Zed is strongest in the mid game, so avoid getting caught alone and group with your allies. Zed falls off in the late game as Ryze gains levels and mana items, so make use of your combos.
Zed.teamfight: Join second, after your allies engage. Spread Ryze E Spell Flux across the frontline and deal area damage with Ryze Q Overload. If Zed enters with Zed R Death Mark, root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison before the mark detonates to reduce the time he has to build up damage. Use Ryze R Realm Warp to move with your allies when disengaging after a team fight.
Zed.watch: Watch the position of Zed W Living Shadow as you move. Step out of the slow area of Zed E Shadow Slash cast from the shadow. If Zed R Death Mark is applied to you, root him with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison before the mark detonates so he can’t build up additional damage.

Zoe.build: Early on, build a core item that increases your mana so you have enough for your combo. Magic resistance helps against Zoe’s magic damage, but Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble reduces your resistance and also deals true damage, so dodging that one hit comes first.
Zoe.combo: To root Zoe, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison. For an all-in, use Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison → Ryze Q Overload → Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload. If Zoe uses Zoe R Portal Jump, make sure to target the spot she started from, where she’ll return.
Zoe.escape: If Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble is also down, close the gap with Ryze R Realm Warp and root her with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Zoe.fight: Right after Zoe uses a spell on the wave, trade briefly with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze Q Overload, then back off. When Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble is down and Zoe R Portal Jump is unavailable, close the gap with Ryze R Realm Warp and look to root her with Ryze E Spell Flux → Ryze W Rune Prison.
Zoe.laning: Early on, prioritize CS and staying on track with your growth over kills. Clear the wave with Ryze E Spell Flux and secure last hits with Ryze Q Overload. Ryze Q Overload is blocked by the first target, so if Zoe is among the minions, wait until she steps out of the wave. Stop trading and focus only on managing the wave if your mana drops below half.
Zoe.phase: Early on, Ryze lacks mana and damage, so watch out for Zoe’s attacks and focus on scaling. In the mid to late game, once you’ve built core items that increase your mana, one full Ryze combo becomes strong, so take advantage of windows when Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble and Zoe R Portal Jump are down.
Zoe.teamfight: After your allies engage, spread marks across the frontline with Ryze E Spell Flux and deal area damage with Ryze Q Overload. If Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble is down, you can approach Zoe with your allies using Ryze R Realm Warp. Watch out for any remaining bubble traps in narrow paths without vision or near objectives, and light up the area with a Control Ward before starting an objective.
Zoe.watch: If Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble hits you, you’ll fall asleep after a short delay and may take a hit from Zoe Q Paddle Star!. If it hits, move behind a wall or an ally before the sleep triggers to get out of Zoe Q Paddle Star!’s angle and range. When Zoe throws Zoe Q Paddle Star! and tries to redirect it, you can interrupt the redirect with Ryze W Rune Prison.
